summary: R253 binds R252 programmable indexed dispatch readiness to the actual current MANAGED index-buffer CPU-shadow values. It converts the live IA byte offset plus StartIndex into an exact shadow element start, scans the exact 16/32-bit index window, and fails closed when any source index falls outside the declared D3D9 MinVertexIndex..MaxVertexIndex range. No DrawIndexed or NativeDrawPath activation is added.

C0_RECOVER.evidence: Recovered GitHub SSOT vr-dx11-native-r71 at 9604cdc394cb711e37adc57a73a631eac8344e3d. Read VR_BACKEND_100_REVIEW_INDEX.md, AGENTS.md, QUEUE_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md, CONVERSION_LANE_STATE.json, prior 00377 run record, VR_AUTODEV/VR_RUN/VR_REVIEW/VR_REGRESSION/VR_PROBLEM history, and Issue #14. R252 is durable and its exact next action selects actual MANAGED source-index value validation.

C1_REVIEW.finding: R252 proves numeric D3D9 indexed arguments and byte windows but does not inspect the actual index values fetched from the current MANAGED IB shadow. Existing NativeManagedIndexRangeReadiness already provides exact generation-bound shadow scanning, and fixed-function R152 proves the pattern. The smallest successor is a programmable R253 receipt that binds those actual values to the R252 snapshot without activating DrawIndexed.

review_lenses.architecture: Reuse NativeManagedIndexRangeReadiness and add one programmable source-value receipt/validator; do not duplicate a second CPU-shadow implementation.
review_lenses.ownership_lifetime: Require the current managed IB mirror snapshot to equal R252 indexBufferSnapshotToken and bind its source-value snapshot/content hash into R253.
review_lenses.stereo_correctness: No WVP/projection/HUD/surface/OpenXR semantics change; runtime remains UNTESTED.
review_lenses.performance: Dormant readiness scan/probe only; no production draw routing or per-frame activation path is enabled.
review_lenses.adversarial: Fail closed on stale/tampered R252 snapshot fields, unsupported index format, unaligned/overflowed IA index offset translation, managed mirror identity drift, and any actual index outside MinVertexIndex..MaxVertexIndex.
